summary_interpretation: Ablation reveals that hydrodynamic wave routing provides decisive timing skill over empirical rainfall accumulation (preventing premature false alarms by ~25.9 hours), while absolute flood stage remains sensitive to uncalibrated bed elevation (z_bed ± 0.25 m). A simplified linear reservoir matches bulk attenuation but misses celerity acceleration.

variants.name: Physical Baseline (Literature n = 0.033)
variants.what_it_proves: Establishes baseline physical routing with Courant stability (C ~ 1.0) and non-negative coefficients.

variants.name: Bed Lower Bound (z_bed - 0.25 m)
variants.what_it_proves: Quantifies stage sensitivity to unresolved river bed elevation: absolute stage shifts ~1:1 with bed datum.

variants.name: Bed Upper Bound (z_bed + 0.25 m)
variants.what_it_proves: Confirms that without surveyed in-situ bathymetry, absolute flood stage inherits direct datum uncertainty.

variants.name: Linear Reservoir + Lag (Bucket Model)
variants.what_it_proves: Tests whether physics beats a bucket: linear reservoir provides comparable peak timing but lacks non-linear wave celerity acceleration during high discharge.

variants.name: Rainfall-Only Threshold (Zero Routing)
variants.what_it_proves: Tests whether routing beats nothing: rainfall-only fires immediately with local rain, lacking the 25.9h hydrodynamic travel time lag required to prevent premature false warnings.
